svg.text: Why the Nyquist column matters as much as the loss

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A 100 m UTP link is a low-pass filter with a corner far below its data rate. 10GBASE-T runs 400 MHz of Nyquist bandwidth through a

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: cable specified only to 500 MHz, and the standard permits 45 dB of loss at the top of that band.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A backplane lane is shorter but its loss is far steeper with frequency. The 10GBASE-KR channel is allowed about 22 dB at 5.16 GHz;

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: at 25G the same board is asked for around 26 dB at 12.9 GHz. Loss that grows with frequency is exactly what an FFE is for, and

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: exactly what makes it amplify noise.
